findings.title: New and changed exit codes (3 and 4) are never asserted
findings.body: This PR makes the exit code the documented, stable contract of the update-compatibility tool (the guide explicitly tells users to rely only on exit codes for automation), changes the recreate exit code from 4 to 3 in CompatibilityResult, and introduces a new exit code 4 for 'feature disabled' — but no test asserts any of these codes. testFeatureNotEnabled only asserts the error message and never checks that the process exits with code 4; testWrongVersions never asserts exit code 3 for the recreate outcome; testCompatible asserts exit code 0 only for the metadata command, not for the subsequent check command; and the feature-disabled path of the check subcommand is not exercised at all. This contract was already wrong once (RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE returned 4 while the docs said 3), so a wiring mistake in picocli.exit(...) or a wrong constant would again ship undetected: CI would stay green while user automation and the operator, both of which consume these exit codes, would break.
